title: Visual Round
blurb: Identify planets, constellations and cosmic objects by sight

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.fact: Saturn's main rings span about 280,000 km yet in places are only about 10 metres thick.

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.fact: Jupiter's coloured bands are clouds of ammonia and water whipped by powerful jet streams.

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.fact: Mars has polar ice caps made of water ice and frozen carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Which world is this?
questions.fact: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water.

questions.question: What type of galaxy is shown here?
questions.fact: Spiral arms glow blue because they are full of young, hot stars.

questions.question: This icy visitor's tail always points away from the…
questions.fact: Solar wind and sunlight push a comet's gas and dust outward, so the tail can even lead the comet.

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.fact: Methane in Uranus's atmosphere absorbs red light, giving it a pale cyan colour.

questions.question: Which planet is this?
questions.fact: Voyager 2 spotted a 'Great Dark Spot' storm on Neptune in 1989.

questions.question: Which constellation is this?
questions.fact: The three stars in a row form Orion's Belt — one of the easiest patterns to spot in the sky.

questions.question: What is this famous star pattern called?
questions.fact: In India this pattern is called Saptarishi, after the seven great sages.

questions.question: This image shows the shadow of a…
questions.fact: The glowing ring is hot gas whose light is bent around the black hole by its gravity.

questions.question: What glowing outer layer of the Sun is revealed during a total solar eclipse?
questions.fact: The corona is over a million degrees — far hotter than the Sun's visible surface.

questions.question: Which constellation is this W-shaped pattern?
questions.fact: Cassiopeia is named after a vain queen in Greek mythology.

questions.question: Seen from India (northern hemisphere), which phase of the Moon is this?
questions.fact: A waxing crescent appears in the western sky just after sunset, a few days after new moon.

questions.question: What kind of object is shown here?
questions.fact: Nebulae glow as nearby hot stars energise their gas, like neon in a sign.
